ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Class: Demonstrative Determiners.

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

4. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

5. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

6. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

8. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

10. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

12. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Class: Adjectives and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
